solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Soon be free maybe? Hour perhaps, or is that too early?

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of the first three words could be arranged some other way

parts.note: an hour is one example of a time

explanation.surface: A prisoner wonders whether release is coming within the hour, or whether that hope is premature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges SOON BE FREE into BEFORE ONES; 'or is that' just leads to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening ahead of its proper moment is said to come prematurely, the idiomatic sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Charge for obstruction to minor work

parts.note: to book someone is to charge them formally with an offence
a let is a hindrance, as in the legal phrase 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A fee is levied for blocking some small piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pamphlet is a slight piece of writing, a small published work.

clue.text: Pam in the classroom?

parts.note: read the answer's two words as instructions: a chart is a map, and flipping those letters gives the girl's name

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a girl named Pam spotted among the pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as wordplay, turns MAP around to give the clue word Pam.
explanation.definitionFit: A large pad of paper on an easel is a standard teaching aid seen in schools and meeting rooms.

clue.text: Storm over main road entering service

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes into the other

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services
the A1 is Britain's longest main road, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A tempest blows over a trunk road leading into a service area.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's main north-south road; the digit 1 stands in as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm is to come down heavily from the sky, as precipitation does; the verb fits as weather.

clue.text: Keep an eye on Republican paper

parts.note: to keep an eye on something is to watch or observe it

explanation.surface: An instruction to watch a newspaper with Republican leanings.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Observer is a well-known British Sunday newspaper, so the title is an example of a paper.

clue.text: Stand for letter by association

parts.note: em is the spelt-out name of the letter M
a body is an organised group or association

explanation.surface: Someone stands as a letter's representative on account of their connection.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand for an idea is to represent or personify it, the verb's sense here.

clue.text: Decently attired, having pocketed cash?

definitions.meaning: wearing proper legwear, hence suitably clothed
British slang for having taken money, often dubiously, into one's possession

explanation.surface: A smartly dressed person with suspiciously full pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both wearing trousers and, in British slang, having pocketed money.

clue.text: Back in Tanzania, same people are found

indicators.note: Back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: In Tanzania the same people turn up again.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maasai are a pastoral ethnic group of Kenya and Tanzania, so they are a people found there.

clue.text: Eager to be occupying temporary accommodation?

parts.note: to occupy a place is to be in it
a tent is shelter put up for a short stay

explanation.surface: Keen to move into somewhere to live for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Being intent on something means being keen and determined about it.

clue.text: Pedigree animal he took away, guzzling one drink

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
took away says the letters of he are removed from the animal

parts.note: a horse is an animal
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A man takes his pedigree animal away and it gulps down a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedigree is a line of descent, one's ancestry or beginnings.

clue.text: Garment for good soul turning in

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: bon is French for good

indicators.note: turning signals the letters of soul are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: An item of clothing for a kind person who is becoming introverted.
explanation.walkthrough: Bon is French; the dictionary blouson is a short jacket bloused at the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: A blouson is a short loose jacket gathered at the waist, a piece of clothing.

clue.text: Braveheart brings good fortune

indicators.note: heart says only the central part of the word for brave is kept

parts.note: plucky means brave

explanation.surface: The film Braveheart is said to bring good fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' strips the outer P and Y from PLUCKY. Braveheart is the 1995 film about William Wallace.
explanation.definitionFit: Luck is chance that goes one's way, the noun synonym for favourable fortune.

clue.text: I presented unsettling order beforehand

indicators.note: unsettling means disturbing the letters of the first two words into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone admits they put forward a disturbing command in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: To predestine is to decree or determine an outcome in advance.

clue.text: Trucker comes from Main Street but isn't in

indicators.note: comes from signals the letters are drawn from the street name and rearranged
isn't says the word in is absent from the street name

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lorry driver rolls in from Main Street but is not at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'isn't in' removes IN from MAIN STREET, leaving MASTREET, which 'comes from' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a teamster is a lorry driver, from the trade union of that name.

clue.text: Sticky greeting changed at the outset on record

indicators.note: changed at the outset says the first letter of the greeting is swapped for another

parts.note: hello is a greeting
to tape something is to put it on record

explanation.surface: An awkward hello whose opening went wrong, now on file.
explanation.walkthrough: The new first letter S is not clued separately; the clue only says the opening changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sellotape is the British brand of clear adhesive tape, the sticky stuff by name.

clue.text: Department returning advice about part of the body

parts.note: an arm is a branch or department of an organisation

indicators.note: returning says the word for advice comes back the other way

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice

explanation.surface: A department sends back its guidance concerning some part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The armpit is the hollow under the shoulder joint, a region of anatomy.

clue.text: Average painter talked about segregation

parts.note: par is the average or normal level

indicators.note: talked about says the painter's name is spoken, giving a word of like sound

parts.note: Titian was the Venetian Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: A middling artist gossiped about in connection with keeping groups apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A partition is a division or separation, such as splitting a country into parts.

clue.text: Spooner will pester associates who are tycoons

indicators.note: Spooner will signals the opening sounds of the two words are swapped, after Rev Spooner

parts.note: to nag is to pester
mates are associates or friends

explanation.surface: A warning that Spooner will bother the colleagues of rich business leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnates are wealthy, powerful business people, the plural synonym for moguls.

clue.text: Put down roots in North Yorkshire town

definitions.meaning: to establish oneself permanently in a place
a market town in the Yorkshire Dales, in the county of North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone makes their home in a town in North Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle is a small market town in the Yorkshire Dales, in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle is to make a permanent home, and it is also the name of a Dales market town.

clue.text: Even that is found in tasteless routine

indicators.note: is found in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: sick humour is tasteless

indicators.note: Even takes the second and fourth letters of the word that

explanation.surface: Even such material turns up in a crude comedy act.
explanation.definitionFit: A shtick is a performer's characteristic gimmick or comic act, a routine.

clue.text: Top civil servant ran admin atrociously!

indicators.note: atrociously means very badly, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that a senior official handled the paperwork terribly.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin is the informal term for a senior, influential government official.

clue.text: Girl adopted by fans of football trickery

indicators.note: adopted by places the girl inside the fans

parts.note: nuts are enthusiasts or fans, as in a golf nut
Meg is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is taken on by supporters of a football club's skilful play.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutmeg is a move in soccer where the ball is played between an opponent's legs, a classic trick.

clue.text: Girl joins Royal Academy, going up to the original dry dock

indicators.note: going up reads the pieces from bottom to top in this down entry

parts.note: Tara is a girl's name
RA is the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A girl is admitted to the Royal Academy and climbs up to an old shipyard.
explanation.walkthrough: Noah's Ark came to rest on Mount Ararat as the flood waters fell.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah's Ark grounded on Mount Ararat, so the mountain was the first place a vessel came to rest on dry land.

clue.text: Our ambient re-recording of drum

indicators.note: re-recording suggests the letters of the two words are laid down again in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A band re-records its ambient track with percussion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tambourine is a small hand drum with jingling metal discs around its frame.

clue.text: Bogged down in Michigan with revolutionary

parts.note: MI is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Michigan
a Red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in Michigan alongside a radical.
explanation.definitionFit: Mired means stuck in mud, and figuratively caught up in difficulty.

clue.text: New opening for charge on deposit

indicators.note: New opening for says the first letter of the word for charge is swapped for another

parts.note: to tilt is to charge with a lance, as jousting knights did

explanation.surface: A bank introduces a fresh fee on savings accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New opening' swaps the T of TILT; the replacement S is not separately clued.
explanation.definitionFit: Silt is fine sediment laid down by water, a deposit in the geological sense.

clue.text: Old man gets to the heart of Holmes' bribe

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

indicators.note: gets to the heart of picks the central letters of the detective's name

explanation.surface: A father uncovers the core of Sherlock Holmes's bribery case.
explanation.definitionFit: To palm someone off with money, or grease a palm, is to pay them a sweetener; palm is used as the verb to bribe.

clue.text: Marauder heard a bawdy song

indicators.note: heard says the words are spoken, giving a like-sounding word

parts.note: a coarse air is a crude tune

explanation.surface: A raider overhears a rude ditty.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair is a pirate, especially of the Barbary coast, a sea raider.

clue.text: Drink today, maybe around 5?

parts.note: tea is a drink
today is an example of a time, the present

explanation.surface: An invitation to take a drink today at about five o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: The British afternoon meal break is traditionally taken at about five o'clock.

clue.text: Master invested recklessly in publicity

indicators.note: recklessly means wildly, so the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A master put money in carelessly to promote something.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertisements are promotional notices, the plural noun for paid publicity.
